title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
statement: You may replace at most `k` characters in `s`. Return the length of the longest substring that can be made of one repeated character.
constraints: s consists of uppercase English letters
hints: A window is valid when its length minus the count of its most frequent character is at most k.
A frequency map of the current window is enough.
The window never needs to shrink by more than it grows, so the best length only increases.

approaches.name: All windows
approaches.explanation: Test the replacement budget on every slice.

approaches.name: Sliding window
approaches.explanation: Grow the right edge and keep the window valid.

editorial: For a window, replacements needed equals length minus the highest frequency inside it. Expand right, update the frequency, and while the window needs more than k replacements, advance left. The maximum valid length is the answer. The most frequent count inside the window is what decides the budget.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def character_replacement(s: str, k: int) -> int:
    count: dict[str, int] = {}
    left = best = max_freq = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        count[ch] = count.get(ch, 0) + 1
        max_freq = max(max_freq, count[ch])
        while (right - left + 1) - max_freq > k:
            count[s[left]] -= 1
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best
